titre: Written context becomes the raw material for agents
essentiel: Figma launches Specs: requirements, design rules and docs in Markdown, wired through MCP.
Several designers place the human approval point at one precise spot rather than everywhere.
Penpot + Codex shows an open path when Figma's MCP quotas block.

syntheses.texte: Figma Specs, tokens as constraints and Dhruv Sood's single spec all say the same thing: an agent does better reading written rules than guessing from an image. Typical AI mistakes (hard-coded value, invented variant, forgotten state) can be caught in review, but are better prevented upstream. The AI for UX round-up adds the flip side: without heuristics, a polished screen hides missing error paths.

syntheses.titre: The agent proposes, the designer approves
syntheses.texte: Three posts put human decision at a precise spot: before bulk application for Rajesh Raote, at PR review for Dhruv Sood, and through a single write-enabled agent for Slsabil Zabady. The disagreement is about complexity: multiplying specialised agents protects, but may cost more than it brings, which Zabady promises to measure.

MCP now connects Figma, Penpot, Codex and in-house tools like Reddit Proto. Vivek Kartha's field report reminds of the friction: free-plan quotas, fonts, debugging. Penpot becomes an open alternative when Figma's limits block, while Figma pushes Specs to keep context in-house.

posts.idee: An agent that asks permission for everything isn't very agentic. Rajesh Raote proposes drawing the line between autonomy and control with three levels: act, show, ask.
concret: ACT: low-risk work the agent does on its own.
SHOW: work it completes but makes visible so the user understands.
ASK: consequential actions that need explicit approval.
Example: an agent writing product copy for 5,000 listings asks for approval when applying in bulk, not at every step.

posts.role: Senior UX Designer at Hewlett Packard Enterprise
posts.idee: Drift comes from the handoff between tools, not from talent. Dhruv Sood has one spec read by all three links: mockup, preview, code.
concret: Claude writes the spec: states, tokens, acceptance checks.
Lovable builds the preview from the same tokens.
Cursor checks each PR against the spec before merge.
AI mistakes caught in review: a hard-coded hex value, an invented 14px gap, a missing error state.
He tracks visual bugs after release and review rounds to sign-off.

posts.role: Senior UI/UX Designer, founder of Uxera
posts.idee: Rather than one agent doing everything, a team of seven specialised agents. Slsabil Zabady tests the idea with Figma, Claude Code and Codex.
concret: Each agent has a role, a persona and permissions: design system analyst, UI architect, Figma builder, QA reviewer.
Only one agent may write to the final design, with explicit approval.
Tests run in sandbox copies, separate from the original screens.
Next post will say whether more agents actually means better results.
posts.commentaires: Open question: one agent or a specialised team?

posts.idee: Figma launches Specs, an open-beta Markdown editor for product requirements, design rules and technical docs.
concret: Documents can be standalone or sit next to designs.
They can include design elements, FigJam diagrams and code blocks.
Through MCP, you pull in context (GitHub, analytics) and push changes back, for example to Linear.
Gradual rollout on paid and education plans.

posts.idee: AI doesn't just need instructions, it needs context. Egberipou Ebeli reads Figma Specs as an answer to that gap.
concret: A screenshot tells an agent what a product looks like; a spec tells it what it should do.
An agent could generate an interface or code from the spec and attached designs.
It could also inspect a finished design to produce technical documentation.

posts.idee: Blocked by the MCP call limit on Figma's free plan, Vivek Kartha redoes his design in Penpot with Codex and keeps an editable file.
concret: Codex creates screens, layouts and reusable components in Penpot through its official, free and open MCP server.
Result: five desktop views, five mobile views and a filter sheet.
Fonts and text wrapping needed fixes, and the setup needed debugging.

posts.role: Founder and Product Designer at Pencil and Screen
posts.idee: Generating UI with AI is easy; keeping it consistent with an existing design system is harder. A design system must also give the AI its constraints.
concret: Risks named: component variants that don't exist, colours outside tokens, inconsistencies across the product.
Approach explored with a client: tokens, explicit rules and validation of generated code.

posts.idee: Polished is not usable. This week's round-up connects the limits of UI generators, grounding in a design system, and the return of hands-on makers.
concret: 2026 study: 138 generated mobile screens (Figma, Banani, Stitch) scored on Nielsen's heuristics; good visual conventions, weak support (errors, recovery).
Reddit Proto, an in-house prototyping tool built on a design system MCP, reportedly reached full adoption with 700+ prototypes.
Transilience case: a solo designer builds a design system after three inconsistent MVPs.
UX job postings reportedly down 71% from the 2022 peak.
